real_s3.explanation: The unit's clearest effect is that it is much weaker when the main subject is dark. Medium or brightly lit subjects drive it far more (rows 19 and 20, d about +1.0, percentiles 98-99), and its similar units are only moderately high there. That effect rests on just 5 dark photos and could not be checked on the new photos, which had only 2 dark ones, so it is a tentative finding. The sharpness preference (row 31) did not hold on new photos (percentile 69), so it is not reliable. The subject-size effect (row 7) could not be checked. Weaker leanings appear toward subjects in the right third, subjects facing left, and warm or neutral rather than cool tints. These are near or below the unusual threshold, partly shared with similar units, or untested, so they are not confident.

real_s1.explanation: The unit fires on the fabric-heavy household classes it was tested on, such as cribs, canopy beds, gowns, quilts and kimonos. Its clearest within-class pattern is being much weaker when the main subject is dark or underexposed. Rows 19 and 20 (d about +1.1 and +0.9, percentiles 99 and 98) are the strongest rows, and the similar units sit lower on them. But they rest on only 5 dark photos, and the new photos had too few dark ones to confirm them, so even these are tentative. The preference for sharp over slightly blurry subjects (row 31) did not hold on new photos. The preference for mid-sized over small subjects (row 7) could not be checked. The weaker response to cool-tinted photos is shared with similar units. The right-third and left-facing rows are near threshold, untested and partly shared, so I don't count them.

real_s2.explanation: The unit fires across bedding, cradle and garment classes (cribs, four-posters, gowns, quilts, kimonos). Its clearest particular signal is suppression when the main subject is dark: medium or bright subjects beat dark ones by about 1 SD, at the 98th to 99th percentile, and similar units do not share this. That evidence rests on only 5 dark photos, and the new photos had too few dark ones (2) to check it. The sharp-over-blurry preference did not replicate (69th percentile on new photos). The preference for a subject filling a moderate part of the frame could not be checked. The leanings toward warm over cool tints, right-third placement and left-facing subjects are weaker, partly shared with similar units, or below the unusual threshold.

null_s2.explanation: The unit is most active on cloth and furniture classes such as cribs, four-posters, gowns, quilts and kimonos. Its clearest particular effect is weaker activity when the main subject is dark: medium or bright lighting beats dark at the 98th to 99th percentile, and no similar unit shares this. That could not be confirmed on new photos because they had only 2 dark photos, so the evidence is real but untested. The preference for sharp over slightly blurry subjects did not replicate (d -0.25 on new photos), so it is likely noise. The preference for subjects filling a moderate share of the frame could not be checked (2 small-subject photos) and was below the 95th percentile anyway. The other effects are weak or shared with similar units: the leftward-facing and right-third placement preferences, and the warm-over-cool tint preference, where similar units are at 98. So the unit is best described as a detector of this bedding/garment class group that is reduced by dark lighting.

The claimed preference for sharp over blurry subjects did not hold on new photos (d -0.25), so it should be dropped. The weaker hints, such as subjects in the right third, left-facing subjects and moderate-sized subjects, are near threshold or partly shared with similar units. The cool-tint dislike is shared with similar units.
